{{short description|American mathematician}}
{{about|the mathematician|the actor|Robert MacNaughton}}
'''Robert Forbes McNaughton, Jr.''' (March 13, 1924 – June 5, 2014) was an American [[mathematician]], [[logician]], and [[computer scientist]] with several key contributions in [[formal languages]], [[grammar (computer science)|grammars]] and [[rewriting system]]s, and [[word combinatorics]].{{r|obit}}

McNaughton was originally from [[Brooklyn]], and earned a bachelor's degree from [[Columbia University]].{{r|obit}}
He completed his Ph.D. at [[Harvard University]]; his dissertation, ''On Establishing the Consistency of Systems'', was supervised by [[Willard Van Orman Quine]].{{r|mgp}}
He taught at the [[University of Pennsylvania]] and then at the [[Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute]].{{r|obit}}

He died in 2014 in [[Troy, New York]].{{r|obit}}
